To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cognitive behavior therapy is an evidence-based treatment for preventing relapse and recurrance in depression, that cognitive behavior therapy can be effective as an acute prophylactic, continuation or sequential cognitive behavior therapy treatment and that cognitive behavior therapy in patients in partial remission after an acute depressive episode can be effective in preventing recurrence of depressive episodes.
Cognitive behavior therapy (CBt) after remission of depression may be an effective alternative treatment for many people who currently use antidepressant medications for years and years.
Cognitive behavior therapy is effective in reducing the risk for relapse in depressed patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of depression, and the prevention of relapsing depression.
the development of relapse prevention strategies for patients with recurrent major depressive disorder (MDD).
the development and evaluation of relapse-prevention programs for depression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cognitive behavior therapy (in all its different forms) is a highly effective and efficient treatment to prevent relapse in patients with recurrent depressive disorder.

the most important ingredients of relapse preventive cognitive behavior therapy are: 1) a cognitive behavioral model of depression; 2) a focus on the patient’s individual vulnerability factors; 3) the use of a cognitive behavioral case formulation; 4) the use of cognitive behavioral techniques (cognitive and behavioral) to address the patient’s individual vulnerabilities.
cognitive behavior therapy is effective in preventing relapse in depression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cognitive behavior therapy is a promising treatment for preventing relapse and relapse prevention in depression, but that the optimal intervention and timing for relapse prevention is still unknown.
relapse prevention cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT-RP) is an effective treatment for patients with recurrent depressive disorder.
cognitive behavior therapy is a very useful intervention in the prevention of relapsee and recurrence in major depressive disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a good idea how to prevent relapse in patients with recurrent depression.
we should be cautious in making generalizations about the effects of psychological interventions in preventing relapse or recurrence of depression.
cognitive behavior therapy (and related psychological interventions) is a crucial component of relapse prevention in depression.
